subject: AcmeBank - eval setup & recommended models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmebank.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeBank - eval setup & recommended models

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Goal: run customer-specific quality/eval runs on Redwood to validate model fit for AcmeBank support summarization and transaction QA use cases. Primary success criteria: accuracy on our labeled prompt set (target: +12% F1 vs baseline), latency under 350ms p50 for interactive flows, and no regressions on safety prompts.

2) Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs included):
   - Redwood-Open-Instruct-7B (best cost/perf for short-form summarization)
   - Llama-2-13B (q4_0) — better long-form coherence, higher cost
   - gptj-6B-clarity — fastest / lowest-cost option to sanity-check throughput

3) Eval assets we need from you: a CSV sample (see attached sample) with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, domain, scoring_type (binary/scale). For complex multi-turn prompts include conversation history rows.

4) Scoring & rubric: we recommend a blended approach — automated similarity (embedding cosine) + BLEU/ROUGE for n-gram alignment + human review for 5% of hardest cases. See attached acme-eval-scoring-criteria.md for the rubric we typically use.

5) Next steps:
   - Sophie: confirm dataset delivery (sample attached) and whether PII redaction is required
   - Acme: tell us preferred privacy controls (VPC/private deployment vs hosted)
   - Redwood: SE will provision an eval job and share a run plan.

Action: Can you upload the full eval CSV to the shared Drive link by EOD Friday 6/18? I’ll loop in Rishi/Neha to schedule the 30-min setup.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: acmebank-eval-dataset-sample.csv, acme-eval-scoring-criteria.md

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AcmeBank - eval setup & recommended models

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications:

- We can get you a 2k-row sample by EOD Friday (6/18). It will include multi-turn examples for the support summarization flow.
- PII: sensitive fields need to be redacted for hosted runs; we may be open to a VPC option if the numbers look good.
- For scoring: we’d like to prioritize factual accuracy over surface-level n-gram overlap. Is your pipeline set up to weight human review more heavily?

If SE needs to do anything special for our dataset format let us know. Also please include estimated token costs for the recommended models so we can budget.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Director, Support Automation
AcmeBank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmebank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeBank - eval setup & recommended models

Thanks Sophie — great, that timeline works. A few notes inline: 

- Redaction: for hosted runs we strongly recommend removing direct identifiers. If you prefer VPC we can provision a private eval; SE will include an estimate in the run plan.

- Scoring weights: yes — we can configure the eval job to use a custom weighting (e.g., 70% embedding-similarity/human + 30% BLEU). We’ll flag the top-10 lowest-scoring cases for human review. Attached is the rubric we use; happy to tweak.

- Token costs (rough estimates per 1M tokens):
   * Redwood-Open-Instruct-7B: $220
   * gptj-6B-clarity: $150
   * Llama-2-13B (q4_0): $480
(These are ballpark; SE will attach a cost projection once we know expected tokens per prompt.)

I’ve attached the sample CSV and scoring doc. Rishi/Neha — can you take point on provisioning the eval job and a run plan? Suggested internal steps below.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AcmeBank - eval setup & recommended models

Looping in details for the eval setup. Internal plan: 

1) Intake & validation (Neha): validate CSV columns (id, prompt, expected_response, domain, scoring_type). Convert multi-turn rows into conversation blocks (JSONL rows per conversation) if present. Reject rows with PII unless redacted.

2) Eval job provisioning (Rishi): create an Eval job in Redwood Console: 
   - Name: acmebank-support-eval-20270618
   - Models: Redwood-Open-Instruct-7B, Llama-2-13B-q4_0, gptj-6B-clarity
   - Metrics: embedding_cosine (primary), BLEU, ROUGE, human_sample_rate=0.05
   - Scoring script: use acme-eval-scoring-criteria.md (basic rubric) and flag low-confidence for human review.

3) Cost projection: run a short 200-row pilot to estimate tokens and latency. Include quantized variants for Llama-2.

4) Security: if Sophie confirms VPC, coordinate with infra for private provisioning. For hosted runs, enforce redaction and minimal retention.

Neha — can you pick up the intake and run validation on the attached sample? I’ll draft the eval job and the pilot plan and share a run timeline.

-Rishi

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmebank.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:45:00 -0700

Hi all —

We validated the 2k-row sample Sophie uploaded to the Drive. Summary of findings: 

- Format: CSV with columns id,prompt,expected_response,domain,scoring_type — PASSED. Multi-turn rows were present and converted to conversation JSONL for the pilot.
- PII: 48 rows had unredacted account numbers; Sophie flagged these and confirmed redaction is in progress (will re-upload by EOD).
- Pilot plan: 200-row pilot scheduled for Mon 6/21. Eval job name acmebank-support-eval-pilot-20270621; models: Redwood-Open-Instruct-7B (baseline), Llama-2-13B-q4_0 (quantized), gptj-6B-clarity.
- Scoring: embedding cosine primary + BLEU + human sample at 5%. Human review UI will surface top-10 lowest-scoring cases per model.

Sophie — once redacted file is uploaded we’ll kick off the pilot and share the cost/time projection. Scheduling invite for a 30-min handoff sent to Sophie/Tom.

-Neha
